raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Summary

**This Ulysses PR is inspired by the idea in [#4903](https://github.com/pytorch/torchtitan/pull/4903).**

Add opt-in Ulysses context parallelism for KDA and GDN. Ulysses moves CP sharding from tokens to heads with packed all-to-all collectives, so each rank processes a full sequence for a subset of heads. Per-head convolution and gate parameters are sliced locally without changing checkpoint keys.

The existing state-routing backends remain the default. Ulysses requires head counts divisible by `TP * CP`. KDA/GDN can share HeadTail or PTRR token load balancing with AllGatherKV full-attention layers: they restore original token order after the input all-to-all and reapply the shared permutation before the output all-to-all. These reorders are local; the contiguous path is unchanged.

```python
ContextParallelTransform(
    inner_attention_map={
        FlexInnerAttention: AllGatherKVFlexInnerAttention,
        InnerGDN: UlyssesInnerGDN,
    }
)
```

For Kimi, map `InnerKDA` to `UlyssesInnerKDA` alongside its MLA CP mapping.

## Performance

Median step time after 5 warmup steps; lower is better. Throughput change is `(state / Ulysses - 1) * 100%`.

### GB300

BF16, full activation rematerialization. CP=4 results use three 20-step repeats; CP=2 uses only the first 20-step run per backend. Discard the first 5 steps of each run.

| Model | CP | Tokens | State ms | Ulysses ms | Throughput | Peak GiB, state / Ulysses |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Kimi K3, 1.46B | 4 | 8K | 896.2 | 983.2 | -8.8% | 11.40 / 11.40 |
| Kimi K3, 1.46B | 4 | 32K | 1061.9 | 1096.0 | -3.1% | 14.30 / 14.40 |
| Qwen3.5-4B | 4 | 8K | 991.9 | 825.9 | +20.1% | 39.74 / 39.73 |
| Qwen3.5-4B | 4 | 32K | 1831.9 | 1960.8 | -6.6% | 39.84 / 39.85 |
| Qwen3.5-35B-A3B text | 2 | 64K (65536) | 13426.3 | 14210.8 | -5.5% | 270.49 / 270.99 |

Kimi 8K was noisy and its backend ordering changed between repeats.

The 35B-A3B run uses two GB300s, TP=EP=1, and replicated parameters (no FSDP), on a fixed synthetic next-token batch. Timings include forward, backward, CP gradient synchronization, clipping, and fused AdamW. Initial weight and input hashes match.

For 35B-A3B, both backends use `PYTORCH_ALLOC_CONF=expandable_segments:True`. Ulysses hit recoverable memory-allocation retries during timed steps near GPU capacity; State did not emit these warnings. The measured difference includes memory pressure and does not isolate CP communication cost.

### H100, larger Qwen

One 20-step run on 8 H100s, TP=2/CP=4, BF16, full activation rematerialization. Paired weight and input hashes match. Both backends use the same `F.conv1d` short-convolution path in this Buck harness.

| Model | Tokens | State ms | Ulysses ms | Throughput | Peak GiB, state / Ulysses | Runs |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---|
| Qwen3.5-9B | 8K | 1288.1 | 1293.0 | -0.4% | 37.19 / 37.19 | [state](https://www.internalfb.com/mlhub/pipelines/runs/mast/torchx-pr5590-qwen35-9b-state-8k-v4-k17nfwht) / [Ulysses](https://www.internalfb.com/mlhub/pipelines/runs/mast/torchx-pr5590-qwen35-9b-ulysses-8k-v3-sfx41vx6) |
| Qwen3.5-9B | 32K | 11102.9 | 11395.6 | -2.6% | 37.33 / 37.34 | [state](https://www.internalfb.com/mlhub/pipelines/runs/mast/torchx-pr5590-qwen35-9b-state-32k-v4-hxpnxkv2) / [Ulysses](https://www.internalfb.com/mlhub/pipelines/runs/mast/torchx-pr5590-qwen35-9b-ulysses-32k-v3-rhjdwd22) |

The backends are not bitwise identical because they evaluate the recurrence and accumulate parameter gradients in different orders. The original 50-batch C4 validation showed comparable loss reduction:

| Model | State, first 10 -> last 10 | Ulysses, first 10 -> last 10 |
|---|---:|---:|
| Kimi K3, 1.46B | 9.7862 -> 6.7734 | 9.7969 -> 6.7715 |
| Qwen3.5-4B | 11.9524 -> 7.6808 | 11.9530 -> 7.6820 |

## Permutation validation

- 86 CPU tests pass, including mixed Kimi K3/Qwen3.5 configuration validation with HeadTail and PTRR.
- A two-GPU BF16 test verifies bitwise-identical outputs, input gradients, and parameter gradients between contiguous and permuted Ulysses KDA/GDN execution. It covers packed document boundaries, non-self-inverse head-tail and arbitrary permutations, and GDN with different Q/K and V head counts. The test is included in the multi-GPU CI lane.
- Ten training steps complete with finite losses and gradient norms for Kimi K3 debug + HeadTail, Kimi K3 debug + PTRR, and Qwen3.5 debug + HeadTail (CP=2, full activation rematerialization, deterministic algorithms).
- Full `pre-commit run --all-files` passes. Existing performance rows above use their original configurations; the added permutation path has not been benchmarked for speed.

nodes.body: Thanks for picking this up! Would it be possible to review and merge my original PR directly? That would keep the history clean. If there's a reason it needs to go through this PR instead, adding me as a co-author on the commit would work too.

Hey @MegaGimen I decided to took it over since we have refactored a lot of code. I was about to leave a comment on your original PR https://github.com/pytorch/torchtitan/pull/4903/, I will add reference to your PR in this PR description! 

Regarding the perf, we didn't see perf gain for this Ulysses CP comparing to the sequence shard CP for linear attention except one small model(Qwen3.5-4B + 8k seqlen). See the perf section in this PR description.

Thanks for the context @acisseJZhong , it makes sense given the refactor. Since the implementation builds on my original PR, would you mind adding a Co-authored-by: Immanuel Sun megagimen@gmail.com trailer to the commit? A reference in the description doesn't show up in the git history. Really appreciate it
And thanks for running the perf comparison, interesting that the gain only shows up on the smaller model.
By the way my perf test is on Qwen3.5-35B-A3B and it doesn't reappear in your side?

added you as an coauthor! @MegaGimen , but to be frank I didn't reference your code if you take a deep look :) Agents already did a good job on this. 

See perf table on Qwen3.5-35B-A3B, it's slightly worse than the attn gym cp we had.
Thanks❤ I may take a look at it because I think the seqlength should not be a variable than impact the perf

@MegaGimen Seqlen IS a variable that will impact the performance and communication amount. Ulysses has a different communication pattern. For a smaller seqlen, while ulysses may have more communication, ulysses doesn't need to do extra metadata computation. But with longer seqlen, the extra communication outweighs the computation saving, hence a worse performance.  For the inter-node experiment, you can see ulysses is always worse because cross-node communication is slower.
What if we do combination of CP? Like one attention that use allgatherkv while another one use ulysses, then permutation should be non-None. I feel this is exception is too restrict.

+class UlyssesInnerKDA(Ulysses[LinearAttentionMetadata], InnerKDA):
+    """Run convolution and KDA on full sequences with CP-sharded heads."""
+
+    @dataclass(kw_only=True, slots=True)
+    class Config(Ulysses.Config, InnerKDA.Config):
+        pass
+
+    def forward(
+        self,
+        query_TC: torch.Tensor,
+        key_TC: torch.Tensor,
+        value_TC: torch.Tensor,
+        raw_gate_THK: torch.Tensor,
+        raw_beta_TH: torch.Tensor,
+        conv_q_weight_C1W: torch.Tensor,
+        conv_k_weight_C1W: torch.Tensor,
+        conv_v_weight_C1W: torch.Tensor,
+        A_log_H: torch.Tensor,
+        dt_bias_HK: torch.Tensor,
+        *,
+        attention_metadata: LinearAttentionMetadata | None,
+    ) -> torch.Tensor:
+        cp_group = spmd_mesh_group(MeshAxisName.CP)
+        if cp_group is None:
+            raise RuntimeError(
+                "Ulysses KDA requires an active multi-rank CP mesh axis."
+            )
+        packed_THF = torch.cat(
+            (
+                query_TC.unflatten(-1, (-1, self.head_dim)),
+                key_TC.unflatten(-1, (-1, self.head_dim)),
+                value_TC.unflatten(-1, (-1, self.head_dim)),
+                raw_gate_THK,
+                raw_beta_TH.unsqueeze(-1),
+            ),
+            dim=-1,
+        )
+        packed_THF = spmd.redistribute(
+            packed_THF, cp_group, src=spmd.S(0), dst=spmd.S(1)
+        )
+        q_THK, k_THK, v_THV, raw_gate_THK, beta_TH1 = packed_THF.split(
+            [self.head_dim] * 4 + [1], dim=-1
+        )
+        # Parameters remain CP-replicated outside this region. Shard their heads
+        # locally; backward contributes zeros for heads owned by other CP ranks.

Regarding the perf, we didn't see perf gain for this Ulysses CP comparing to the sequence shard CP for linear attention except one small model(Qwen3.5-4B + 8k seqlen). See the perf section in this PR description.

And thanks for running the perf comparison, interesting that the gain only shows up on the smaller model.
By the way my perf test is on Qwen3.5-35B-A3B and it doesn't reappear in your side?

added you as an coauthor! @MegaGimen , but to be frank I didn't reference your code if you take a deep look :) Agents already did a good job on this. 

See perf table on Qwen3.5-35B-A3B, it's slightly worse than the attn gym cp we had.
Thanks❤ I may take a look at it because I think the seqlength should not be a variable than impact the perf

@MegaGimen Seqlen IS a variable that will impact the performance and communication amount. Ulysses has a different communication pattern. For a smaller seqlen, while ulysses may have more communication, ulysses doesn't need to do extra metadata computation. But with longer seqlen, the extra communication outweighs the computation saving, hence a worse performance.  For the inter-node experiment, you can see ulysses is always worse because cross-node communication is slower.
